$comment: Allowlist for scripts/check-scan-findings.mjs, the gate over the scanners that run
outside the JS test suite: Trivy image and IaC scans, and the ZAP baseline, in
.github/workflows/security-scanning.yml.
The grammar is the same as scripts/semgrep-allowlist.json on purpose. A finding at
or above the job's severity floor with no entry fails CI. An entry past its expiry
fails CI even though the finding still matches, so an acceptance cannot outlive the
triage that justified it. An entry that matches nothing fails CI as stale.
"scanner" is "trivy" or "zap" and scopes the entry to one report, so a ZAP alert
can never excuse a Trivy CVE that happens to share its number. Omit "locations"
to accept a finding wherever it appears. For Trivy each value is matched as a
substring of the finding's location, which is "<target>:<package>@<version>" for a
vulnerability and the scanned path for a misconfiguration.
A ZAP alert becomes one finding per instance it lists, and every one of them has to
match. Its "id" is the alert reference, such as 10055-4, not the plugin id: plugin
10055 alone raises a dozen different Content-Security-Policy alerts, and accepting one
must not accept the rest. Each ZAP "locations" value is an absolute URL with no query
or fragment. It covers a URL on the same origin whose path is its path or continues it
past a "/", whatever the query, so /api-docs covers /api-docs/streaming but not
/api-docs-internal. ZAP lists only five URLs for an alert it marks systemic, so an
entry scoped by "locations" vouches for the URLs the report shows and no others.
One alert reference can still cover more than its reason reviewed, so a ZAP entry can
pin what each instance reports. "otherinfo" has to equal a whole line of the
instance's other info: 10055-4 is raised for any directive that admits every host,
and that line lists which. "evidence" lists substrings, and the instance's evidence
has to contain one of them: for 90003 the evidence is the tag that lacks integrity.
Any other key in an entry fails CI, so a misspelled "locations", "otherinfo" or
"evidence" cannot leave the entry accepting every instance of its id.

entries.reason: img-src admits any https: origin, and "otherinfo" limits this entry to that one directive. The page still shows images from hosts the product does not choose: a reply image once the reader presses Load image, search and citation favicons the provider supplies (CitationChip.tsx, WebSearchCard.tsx, ResearchPanel.tsx), connector directory icons (DirectoryGrid.tsx, ConnectorDetailView.tsx) and map tiles from AGI_MAP_TILE_URL_TEMPLATE. Model output no longer reaches the directive unasked. MarkdownImage (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx) fetches on its own only same-origin, data: and blob: sources and the exact URLs of the turn's own search results and citations; any other host renders as a placeholder that names it and loads, with no referrer, only when the reader clicks. MermaidDiagram refuses a diagram whose image nodes, actor icons or styles would fetch from another site. A pass-through same-origin image proxy would clear this alert while still fetching the same URLs server-side, and it would add SSRF surface, so the directive keeps https: until those hosts are served through a vetted path.

style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' because a nonce covers style elements, not style attributes: apps/web and packages/ui render about 2,300 React style props across 215 components, and Clerk documents 'unsafe-inline' as required for its components to inject their styles (clerk.com/docs/guides/secure/best-practices/csp-headers, read 2026-10-01). script-src stays nonce-only, which scripts/check-security-response-headers.mjs enforces. The exemption is disclosed on /security and pinned by apps/web/app/trust/posture-claims.test.ts.

Both flagged tags are Clerk's, served from its Frontend API host: @clerk/nextjs renders clerk-js (/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@6/dist/clerk.browser.js) and preloads @clerk/ui (/npm/@clerk/ui@1/dist/ui.browser.js) with no integrity attribute. Each URL names a major version Clerk updates in place, so no fixed hash can match it. "evidence" limits the entry to those two paths on clerk-ci.invalid, the host the scan's placeholder publishable key decodes to, so any other cross-origin script or preload without integrity still fails. First-party scripts are same-origin and outside this alert. Removing the CDN load means bundling @clerk/clerk-js and @clerk/ui into the build, a dependency change.

Public code samples, not server source. /api-docs renders the SDK examples in apps/web/content/api-docs/code-samples.json (the evidence is their 'for chunk in stream:'), and /gallery/<id> renders the fixed examples in apps/web/app/gallery/inspiration.ts (python-data-pipeline, sql-user-accounts-schema). Both pages exist to show code. Scoped to those two paths, so the same alert on any other URL still fails.

The sign-in form declares method="post" only so that a submission no script handled can never write the password into the address bar (apps/web/features/auth/AuthEmailStep.tsx). The page has no POST handler: every credential goes from the browser to the identity provider through its own SDK, which carries its own request protection, so there is no state-changing request to this origin for a forged form to trigger. Scoped to /login, so the same alert on any other form still fails.
